perspective:
John Atcitty’s available information:

- He knows he is a Heavy Equipment Operator and teaches equipment operation at a community center. Beverly Yan is his colleague there and teaches adult education classes; they collaborate on practical/theoretical projects.
- He knows his own education level is middle school and is aware Beverly has a doctorate. During their joint class project, this made him feel insecure.
- He set up equipment for a demonstration and told Beverly he hoped it met her expectations. He heard Beverly say she has always admired how he handles machines, that education isn’t just about degrees, and that it’s about what you can do with what you know.
- After Beverly praised his machinery expertise, he felt more confident. He thanked her and proposed a new workshop combining theory and practice. Beverly said she loved the idea, that his practical skills are invaluable, and that they could create something special together.
- After a successful collaboration, he worried Beverly might have higher expectations and felt pressured. He told her he might not always meet their recent high standards. Beverly appreciated his honesty, suggested realistic goals, and said their combined efforts—not perfection—make projects successful.
- After their frank discussion, he believed Beverly valued his honesty and saw him as a reliable partner, which increased his sense of worth. He told her he felt he could be open with her. Beverly said she respected his openness, trusted his judgment completely, and wanted to keep transparency going.
- Encouraged by their collaborations and mutual respect, he felt ambitious and proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase their projects. Beverly called it fantastic, said it was the perfect way to demonstrate their impact, and agreed to start planning.
